middle_english: What, why dedyst thou wynk whan thou a wyf toke?
By a good howsbande thys tale shal be tolde.
He weddyd a womane that was fayre and bolde.
She dyde mor then sho myght withyn her owne wone.
How wold yow have me doo mor then I cane?
tend I to owr goslyngs that gothe on the grene.
Alle thys wold a good howsewyfe do long ar het were prime;
Put smal feyre ondernethe, sir, for Godes sake;
Sche callyd to her lade, and to the plow they wend;
And that schall helpe thee in thy peyne.
Ne laughe thou not low, be thou therof sore.
That hem hath holpen whan that they were seeke.
To take oure wey ther as I yow devyse.
And eek in what array that they were inne;
And at a knyght than wol I first bigynne.
At Alisaundre he was whan it was wonne.
No Cristen man so ofte of his degree.
At many a noble armee hadde he be.
In lystes thries, and ay slayn his foo.
And of his port as meeke as is a mayde.
In al his lyf unto no maner wight.
His hors were goode, but he was nat gay.
With lokkes crulle as they were leyd in presse.
Of twenty yeer of age he was, I gesse.
In hope to stonden in his lady grace.
Al ful of fresshe floures, whyte and reede.
Syngynge he was, or floytynge, al the day;
He was as fressh as is the month of May.
Short was his gowne, with sleves longe and wyde.
Wel koude he sitte on hors and faire ryde.
Juste and eek daunce, and weel purtreye and write.
And carf biforn his fader at the table.
And he was clad in cote and hood of grene.
And in his hand he baar a myghty bowe.
A not heed hadde he, with a broun visage.
Of wodecraft wel koude he al the usage.
Harneised wel and sharp as point of spere;
A Cristopher on his brest of silver sheene.
An horn he bar, the bawdryk was of grene;
A forster was he, soothly, as I gesse.
That of hir smylyng was ful symple and coy;
Hire gretteste ooth was but by Seinte Loy;
For Frenssh of Parys was to hire unknowe.
At mete wel ytaught was she with alle;
Ne wette hir fyngres in hir sauce depe;
That no drope ne fille upon hire brest.
In curteisie was set ful muchel hir lest.
Of grece, whan she dronken hadde hir draughte.
Kaught in a trappe, if it were deed or bledde.
Or if men smoot it with a yerde smerte;
Hir mouth ful smal, and therto softe and reed.
It was almoost a spanne brood, I trowe;
Ful fetys was hir cloke, as I was war.
A manly man, to been an abbot able.
Ther as this lord was kepere of the celle.
And heeld after the newe world the space.
This is to seyn, a monk out of his cloystre.
But thilke text heeld he nat worth an oystre;
As Austyn bit? How shal the world be served?
Lat Austyn have his swynk to hym reserved!
Grehoundes he hadde as swift as fowel in flight;
Was al his lust, for no cost wolde he spare.
With grys, and that the fyneste of a lond;
He hadde of gold ywroght a ful curious pyn;
